title: Complete the Small Sudoku

concept.title: Fill the empty cells in order, and check three rules for each digit
body: A small sudoku is a 4 by 4 board with digits 1 to 4. Every row, every column and each of the four 2 by 2 boxes must contain each digit exactly once. Some cells are given (digits 1 to 4) and the empty cells are `0`. The search walks over the cells in reading order. A given cell is simply checked; an empty cell tries the digits 1 to 4, and a digit is allowed if **no other cell of its row, column or box** already has it.

Because the check looks at **all** other cells (also the given ones that come later in the order), a digit that clashes with a later given is rejected at once, and a board whose given digits already clash with each other has no completion: the check of a given cell fails, and the count is 0. Cells that are filled by the search are set back to 0 afterwards (**unchoose**).

statement: A 4 by 4 sudoku board is partly filled with the digits 1 to 4; an empty cell is written as `0`. A completed board has every digit 1 to 4 exactly once in every row, every column and every 2 by 2 box (the four boxes are formed by rows 1-2 and 3-4 and columns 1-2 and 3-4). Count the ways to fill the empty cells. If the given digits already clash, the answer is 0.
inputFormat: 4 lines with 4 characters each: the digits 0 to 4 without spaces.

examples.note: With a single digit given, there are 288 / 4 = 72 completions.

hints: Number the cells 0 to 15 in reading order and solve cell by cell.
A digit is allowed if no other cell in the same row, column or box has it.
Check the given cells as well, so that contradictory givens give 0.

solution.complexity: Time tiny (at most a few hundred completions), space O(1).
